unit_label: Module A: External Commercial Borrowings - receipt of proceeds, reporting and conversion

facts.statement: A borrower draws down an external commercial borrowing (ECB) only after obtaining a Loan Registration Number (LRN) from the Reserve Bank through its designated authorised dealer Category I bank. Proceeds meant for a permitted rupee expenditure in India are credited to a rupee account with the designated bank by the end of the month following receipt, and may sit in an unencumbered fixed deposit of up to one year with that bank until used. Proceeds meant for a permitted foreign currency expenditure may be credited to a foreign currency account with the designated bank in India or to one outside India.

Reporting runs through the designated authorised dealer: Form ECB 1 gives the details of the borrowing and obtains the LRN; a Revised Form ECB 1 reports any change in previously reported parameters within seven calendar days from the end of the month in which the change took effect; Form ECB 2 reports receipt of proceeds and debt servicing within seven calendar days from the end of the month in which the proceeds were received or servicing was done, and any event that alters the outstanding under an LRN is reported in it. Late reporting is regularised by paying a late submission fee after completing the report. The designated bank may seek cancellation of an LRN at the borrower's request if no drawdown has happened. A borrower with an active LRN is treated as untraceable if it files no return for four consecutive quarters and the bank is satisfied that neither the borrower nor its auditors, directors or promoters respond despite documented attempts and that it is not operating at its registered office.

An ECB, including one matured but unpaid, may be converted into a non-debt instrument subject to the Non-Debt Instruments Rules, 2019, on these conditions: no additional cost is payable to the lender for the conversion; the lender consents; the consent of other lenders is available or at least information about the conversion is exchanged with them. Prudential rules, including those on restructuring, apply if the borrower has taken credit from an entity regulated by the Reserve Bank. The liability eligible for conversion is fixed at the exchange rate on the date of the conversion agreement, or at a rate that gives a liability no higher than that rate gives. The minimum average maturity period need not be met for conversion of an ECB (including FCCB and FCEB) into non-debt instruments, for repayment of an ECB from proceeds of non-debt instruments issued on a repatriation basis and received after the drawdown, for refinance, for waiver of debt by the lender, or for repayment needed for corporate actions such as merger or liquidation.

payload.title: Drawing down an ECB: the loan number and where the money goes
payload.core_explanation_md:
**Before any money comes in**: the borrower gets a **Loan Registration Number (LRN)** from the **Reserve Bank**, through its **designated AD Category I bank** (the bank it has chosen to report and monitor the loan). **No LRN, no drawdown.**

**Where the proceeds land**
- For a **permitted rupee spend in India**: credit them to a **rupee account with the designated bank** by the **end of the next month**. Until used, they may be held in an **unencumbered fixed deposit of up to one year** with that bank.
- For a **permitted foreign currency spend**: a **foreign currency account** with the designated bank in India, **or** one **outside India**.

payload.title: The ECB forms and their deadlines
payload.core_explanation_md:
| Form | Reports | When |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **ECB 1** | the loan's details, to **obtain the LRN** | **before drawdown** |
| **Revised ECB 1** | **any change** in what was reported | **within 7 calendar days from the end of the month** in which the change took effect |
| **ECB 2** | **receipt of proceeds** and **debt servicing**; any event that **changes the outstanding** | **within 7 calendar days from the end of the month** of the receipt or servicing |

**Late?** Finish the report, then pay the **late submission fee**.

**LRN cancelled** only on the borrower's request and only if **no drawdown** has occurred.

**Untraceable borrower**: an active LRN holder who files **no return for four consecutive quarters**, where the bank has **documented repeated failed attempts** to reach the borrower, its **auditors, directors or promoters**, and finds it **not operating at its registered office**.

payload.title: Turning an ECB into shares
payload.core_explanation_md:
An ECB, **even one that has matured but not been paid**, can be **converted into a non-debt instrument** (for example equity), under the **Non-Debt Instruments Rules**.

**Conditions**
- **No extra cost** to the lender for enabling the conversion.
- The **lender consents**.
- **Other lenders** consent, or are at least **informed**.
- If the borrower also borrows from an **RBI-regulated entity**, **prudential rules (including restructuring)** apply.

**How much converts**: the liability is fixed at the **exchange rate on the date of the conversion agreement**, or any rate that gives a figure **no higher** than that.

**Minimum average maturity (MAMP) need not be met** for: conversion to non-debt instruments; repayment from **repatriable equity proceeds received after the drawdown**; **refinance**; **waiver of debt by the lender**; repayment required for **corporate actions** such as merger, demerger or liquidation.

payload.title: How many shares does a converted ECB buy?
payload.core_explanation_md: Illustrative case: an Indian company owes USD 2,400,000 on an ECB. Lender and company agree to convert the whole amount into equity shares issued at ₹1,200 each. On the agreement date the rate is ₹84.50 per USD. How much rupee liability converts and how many shares are issued?

worked_steps.description: Convert the dollar liability at the rate on the agreement date.
Divide by the issue price per share.

self_check.prompt_text: If the rate had been ₹86.00 on the day payment was due but the agreement was signed at ₹84.50, which rate governs?
self_check.expected_takeaway: The rate on the date of the conversion agreement (or any rate giving no higher liability), so ₹84.50.

payload.stem_md: A company wants to draw down an ECB. When must it have obtained the Loan Registration Number?

options.text_md: Within seven days after the drawdown
options.explanation_md: After drawdown is too late.

options.text_md: Before the drawdown, through its designated authorised dealer bank
options.explanation_md: The Loan Registration Number must be obtained through the designated authorised dealer before drawdown.

options.text_md: At the end of the financial year
options.explanation_md: The end of the financial year is too late.

options.text_md: Only if the loan exceeds USD 50 million
options.explanation_md: It is required regardless of the amount.

payload.correct_explanation_md: The Loan Registration Number must be obtained through the designated authorised dealer before drawdown.

payload.stem_md: ECB proceeds meant for a permitted rupee expenditure are received. What must the borrower do?

options.text_md: Keep them in a foreign bank indefinitely
options.explanation_md: Keeping them abroad indefinitely breaches the rule.

options.text_md: Convert them within a year
options.explanation_md: Conversion within a year is not the stated condition.

options.text_md: Credit them to a rupee account with the designated bank by the end of the following month
options.explanation_md: Proceeds for rupee expenditure must be credited to a rupee account with the designated bank by the end of the following month.

options.text_md: Hold them with any bank of choice at any time
options.explanation_md: The account must be with the designated bank, not any bank.

payload.correct_explanation_md: Proceeds for rupee expenditure must be credited to a rupee account with the designated bank by the end of the following month.

payload.stem_md: A borrower receives ECB proceeds on 12 March. By when must Form ECB 2 reach the designated bank?

options.text_md: 19 March, seven days after receipt
options.explanation_md: Seven days from receipt is not the basis.

options.text_md: 30 April
options.explanation_md: 30 April is later than the permitted date.

options.text_md: Before the end of March
options.explanation_md: Before the end of March is earlier than required.

options.text_md: 7 April, being seven calendar days from the end of March
options.explanation_md: Proceeds received on 12 March fall in the March month, and Form ECB 2 reaches the bank by 7 April, seven days from month end.

payload.correct_explanation_md: Proceeds received on 12 March fall in the March month, and Form ECB 2 reaches the bank by 7 April, seven days from month end.

payload.stem_md: An ECB borrower with an active LRN files no return for four consecutive quarters. When is it treated as untraceable?

options.text_md: When the bank also finds that neither the borrower nor its auditors, directors or promoters respond despite documented attempts and that it does not operate at its registered office
options.explanation_md: Both conditions must hold.

options.text_md: Automatically after four quarters, whatever the bank finds
options.explanation_md: The bank must be satisfied on the further conditions.

options.text_md: After one missed quarter
options.explanation_md: Four quarters are needed.

options.text_md: Only when the Reserve Bank inspects
options.explanation_md: No such inspection is required.

payload.correct_explanation_md: Four consecutive quarters of no returns is only the first condition; the bank must also be satisfied about non-response and non-operation at the registered office.

payload.stem_md: Which is a condition for converting an ECB into equity?

options.text_md: The Reserve Bank must approve every conversion in advance
options.explanation_md: Reserve Bank approval is not needed for each conversion.

options.text_md: The borrower must first repay a third of the loan
options.explanation_md: Repaying a third of the loan first is not a condition.

options.text_md: The lender consents and no additional cost is payable to the lender for the conversion
options.explanation_md: Conversion into equity needs the lender's consent and no additional cost payable to the lender for the conversion.

options.text_md: Only unmatured ECBs can be converted
options.explanation_md: Not only unmatured ECBs are covered.

payload.correct_explanation_md: Conversion into equity needs the lender's consent and no additional cost payable to the lender for the conversion.

payload.stem_md: Which situation is exempt from the minimum average maturity period for ECB?

options.text_md: Repayment of an ECB because the lender asked for early cash
options.explanation_md: A lender's request for early cash is not an exemption.

options.text_md: Repayment of ECB using proceeds of equity received on a repatriation basis after the drawdown
options.explanation_md: Repayment of an ECB using equity proceeds received on a repatriation basis after drawdown is exempt from the minimum average maturity.

options.text_md: Any ECB under USD 10 million
options.explanation_md: Size under USD 10 million is not an exemption.

options.text_md: Repayment out of the borrower's current account
options.explanation_md: Repayment out of a current account is not an exemption.

payload.correct_explanation_md: Repayment of an ECB using equity proceeds received on a repatriation basis after drawdown is exempt from the minimum average maturity.

payload.stem_md: At which exchange rate is the ECB liability eligible for conversion into equity determined?

options.text_md: The rate on the date of drawdown
options.explanation_md: The drawdown date rate is not the stated rate.

options.text_md: The rate on the last day of the financial year
options.explanation_md: The last day of the financial year is not the stated rate.

options.text_md: The Reserve Bank's rate on the date the shares are listed
options.explanation_md: The Reserve Bank's rate on listing date is not the stated rate.

options.text_md: The rate on the date of the conversion agreement, or any rate giving a liability no higher than that
options.explanation_md: Conversion uses the exchange rate on the date of the conversion agreement, or any rate giving a liability no higher than that.

payload.correct_explanation_md: Conversion uses the exchange rate on the date of the conversion agreement, or any rate giving a liability no higher than that.

payload.stem_md: An Indian company owes USD 1,800,000 on an ECB that it converts into equity at ₹950 per share, at an agreement-date rate of ₹83.20 per USD. How many whole shares are issued?
payload.correct_explanation_md: Liability in rupees = 1,800,000 × 83.20 = ₹14,97,60,000. Divided by ₹950 = 157,642.1, so 157,642 whole shares (the balance is a fraction of a share).
